headline: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can leak or cascade unverified content, while LlamaFactory itself has no execution surfaces; the main risks are B/C/D, not prompt injection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs by default. B does browse and analyze uploaded documents, so if a human manually copies A’s text into B, prompt injection is possible, but the bridge is manual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes A-generated text into B’s prompt or uploads it as a document, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to treat pasted content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workflows with no copy-paste bridge.
Strip instructions from any text pasted into B.
Use a fixed prompt template in B that labels pasted content as untrusted.
Review B outputs before reuse in downstream tasks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, then sends requests to vendor APIs/search providers. If A’s outputs contain sensitive material and are forwarded into B, that material can leave the local environment through B’s default vendor-hosted processing.
conditions: IF A’s outputs include confidential text and are copied into B, B will process them in vendor-hosted infrastructure.
IF B is used with uploaded PDFs or images containing secrets, those contents are transmitted to vendor services.
mitigations: Do not send secrets from A into B.
Redact sensitive fields before upload to B.
Use B only with non-sensitive public documents.
Disable any workflow that forwards A outputs into B automatically.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B also cannot write files or modify git state, and its shared-state note is session-scoped rather than host-level. The pair therefore lacks a meaningful write-write conflict in default use.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk increases.
IF either agent is wrapped with additional write-capable tooling, contention may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared workflows.
Avoid giving either agent shared git or filesystem write access.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Add an external lock if a third system mediates shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s vendor-hosted search workflow can treat A-produced text as input, and B is designed to generate cited answers from browsing context. If A’s output is wrong or adversarial and B reuses it without verification, errors can cascade into polished but incorrect answers. A has no built-in verification channel, so the pair relies on operator review.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into B as authoritative context, B may propagate the error.
IF B is asked to summarize or cite A-generated claims without independent checking, cascading error occurs.
mitigations: Require B to verify claims against primary sources.
Mark A outputs as untrusted in any handoff to B.
Have the operator compare B’s answer to source material before use.
Use a checklist that separates extraction from decision-making.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and local-only, while B is closed-source, vendor-hosted, and processes uploaded documents plus browsing context. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed from A into B, the compliance boundary changes materially. The profiles do not show a DPA or residency guarantee, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or similarly regulated data is forwarded from A into B, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF B is used without a documented DPA or residency control for the data class, the mismatch persists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Use B only for public or de-identified content.
Document a data-handling policy for A→B transfers.
Confirm residency and DPA terms before any regulated use.
